source_defaults.notes: Candidate-controlled text from actual retained campaign versions. Unknown original publication is not replaced with an archive request date. Campaign statements and projected effects are not independent factual findings.

sources.speaker: Julie Oliver
sources.notes: Publisher compilation is explicitly dated January8,2020 on its pages. The month identifies the dated edition without inventing a first-publication day from the2025 archive. Oliver's rows were visually matched to the candidate-name column. The implausibly repeated Sloan rows, which duplicate Doggett's answer, are withheld; they are not used as Sloan's statements.

statements.quote: I support the Medicare for All of 2019 bill
statements.claim: Supports the2019 Medicare for All bill and the Disability Integration Act, including community-based care and accessible integrated housing.

statements.quote: covering all medically necessary care for LGBTQ+ patients under Medicare for All
statements.claim: Explicitly supports Medicare for All coverage, including medically necessary LGBTQ care; the complete visually verified row supplies the context.
Supports the Equality Act and protections against housing discrimination, alongside disability and tenant rights.

statements.quote: LGBTQIA+ Americans are entitled to full federal equality.
statements.claim: Answers yes to the Equality Act question and explicitly supports equal federal treatment. The row was checked against the rendered candidate-name column, not inferred from plain-text name order.

statements.quote: rejecting ALL corporate donations and developer dollars
statements.claim: States a campaign funding restriction on corporate and developer money. This is a pledge, not an independent campaign-finance audit.

statements.quote: doesn't take a single dime from any PACs or special interest groups
statements.claim: States an all-PAC funding restriction, broader in its stated category than a corporate-PAC-only restriction. No actual receipt totals are inferred.
Names the Green New Deal among her campaign commitments, alongside Medicare for All and workers' rights.
Names the Green New Deal in her campaign platform. This April archive does not by itself prove the exact page version before the March primary.

statements.quote: millions of new beautiful, publicly-owned homes
statements.claim: Supports the Homes For All Act and Green New Deal public-housing investment, not merely generic housing affordability.

statements.quote: 3% a year or 1.5 times the Consumer Price Index (whichever is higher)
statements.claim: Proposes the higher of3% or1.5 times CPI as a national rent-increase cap, with an improvement waiver. This is not the lower-of formula found in another race's questionnaire.

statements.quote: one boot in office fighting for legislative changes, and one boot in the movement
statements.claim: Describes governing through both legislative action and grassroots organizing, rather than elections alone.

comparisons.analysis: Both expressly support Medicare for All. Sloan's own archived healthcare page supplies her position; the defective repeated survey rows are not used.
Both support the Equality Act. Sloan's position is verified on her own archived housing page, independently of the problematic publisher compilation.

Sloan pledges to reject corporate and developer money; Oliver states an all-PAC restriction. These stated donor categories differ, but the comparison does not assert that Sloan actually accepted any particular PAC contribution.
Both available campaign versions affirm a Green New Deal. Oliver's exact retained issues-page version is post-primary and the comparison remains explicitly timing-qualified.
